title: Northbeam TechWorks Scheduling Note: The Day Whose Percent Governs a Surcharge
content:
The day whose surcharge percent is read on a Northbeam TechWorks Installation and Repair job is settled first, before any percent is looked up.

- Where the slot booked for the job has been moved at least once since the work was asked for and the job carries labour for two or more attendances, the surcharge percent is read for the day of the latest attendance carrying labour.
- Where the slot has never been moved, the surcharge percent is read for the day the slot stands booked for.
- Where neither of those situations holds, the surcharge percent is read for the day the surcharge is booked.

Two facts of the job settle which reading governs: how many times the slot has been moved since the work was asked for, and how many labour entries stand on the job. The day of the latest attendance carrying labour is the attendance day of the most recent labour entry standing on the job.

## Reading the three situations

| The slot has been moved | Labour entries standing on the job | The day whose percent is read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| at least once | two or more | the day of the latest attendance carrying labour |
| never | any | the day the slot stands booked for |
| at least once | fewer than two | the day the surcharge is booked |

The middle line turns on the slot never having been moved at all, and holds however many labour entries stand on the job. The last line is what remains: the slot has been moved, but the job does not carry labour for two or more attendances.

## Illustrations on hypothetical jobs

**A slot moved twice, three labour entries.** The first situation governs, and the day read is the attendance day of the most recent labour entry — which need not be the day the slot now stands booked for.

**A slot never moved, four labour entries.** The second situation governs, because the slot has never been moved, and the day read is the day the slot stands booked for, whatever the attendance days of the labour entries.

**A slot moved once, one labour entry.** Neither of the first two situations holds, and the day read is the day the surcharge is booked.
